solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Analyst flustered beginning to engage this sporty chap

indicators.note: flustered means thrown into confusion, so the letters of the fodder are jumbled
the beginning of the word engage is its first letter

explanation.surface: An analyst gets flustered as some athletic man starts to get involved.
explanation.walkthrough: 'beginning to' gives E from 'engage'; 'flustered' shuffles E with THIS SPORTY CHAP.
explanation.definitionFit: A therapist practising psychoanalysis is commonly called an analyst.

clue.text: Reproduction Stonehenge assembled in capital

indicators.note: in places the rearranged stones within the city name

parts.note: Paris is the capital of France

indicators.note: assembled means put together, so the letters of Stonehenge are rearranged

explanation.surface: A reproduction of the ancient monument is put together in a capital city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'assembled' shuffles STONEHENGE into THENOGENES, which goes 'in' PARIS. 'Reproduction' looks like a replica, but it is the biological sense.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the biological term for reproduction from an unfertilised egg, without a male.

clue.text: Food unusually tough and extremely rubbery

indicators.note: unusually signals the letters appear in an uncommon order
the extremes of a word are its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A complaint about food that is oddly tough and very rubbery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'extremely' takes R and Y from 'rubbery'; 'unusually' shuffles them with TOUGH.
explanation.definitionFit: This fermented milk product is a food, the setter's broad category.

clue.text: Military vehicle brings force in to stop pain

indicators.note: the clue says force is brought in, so F goes inside the word for stop

parts.note: to halt is to stop
F is the physics abbreviation for force
to rack is to cause great pain, as on the torture rack

explanation.surface: An army vehicle brings in troops to end suffering.
explanation.definitionFit: A half-track is an army vehicle with wheels at the front and tracks at the rear.

clue.text: Incline encountered after time in hike

indicators.note: the slope is met after the time letter, so it follows in the answer

parts.note: a ramp is a sloping incline

explanation.surface: A walker meets a slope after a while on a long walk.
explanation.definitionFit: To tramp is to make a long walk, a synonym of hike.

clue.text: Such surveys necessarily on the way out?

definitions.text: Such surveys necessarily on the way out?

parts.words: Such surveys necessarily on the way out?
parts.note: voters are questioned as they leave the polling station, so these surveys are taken literally on the way out

explanation.surface: A wry suggestion that some kind of survey is in decline.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on the way out' reads as obsolete, but it means literally leaving the polling station.
explanation.definitionFit: These election-day surveys question voters as they leave after casting ballots.

clue.text: Sign that character must be removed by alpha female

parts.note: alpha is A in the NATO alphabet

parts.words: Sign that character must be removed
parts.note: dele is the proofreader's mark telling the printer to delete a character

explanation.surface: A proofreading instruction applied by a dominant woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dele' is the Latin-derived proofreading mark meaning delete.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a woman's given name, as borne by the singer, so a female.

clue.text: His name is love

parts.note: to adore someone is to love them

explanation.surface: A romantic declaration that a man's name is love itself.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a man's given name, so it is his name in the clue.

clue.text: Face up to defeat when punch gets through?

definitions.meaning: to accept a setback bravely and without complaint
a boxer's blow landing on the jaw, the literal sense of the idiom

explanation.surface: Accept losing when a blow finally lands.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means accepting misfortune stoically, coming from a boxer absorbing a blow to the jaw.

clue.text: Excellent beer sent round in Crown & Sceptre?

indicators.note: sent round means turned about, so the combined letters are read backwards

parts.note: A1 means excellent, written here as AI
lager is a type of beer

explanation.surface: Fine ale served at a pub named the Crown & Sceptre.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crown & Sceptre' looks like a pub name; it is an example of royal insignia, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: Crown and sceptre are examples of the ceremonial emblems of royalty.

clue.text: Maybe swelling number of reserve forwards

parts.note: to put something on ice is to keep it in reserve
in rugby the forwards are collectively the pack

explanation.surface: A rugby team's number of substitute forwards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'number' is read as numb-er, something that numbs, here applied to a swelling.
explanation.definitionFit: A cold compress numbs pain, so it is a thing that deadens, maybe for swelling.

clue.text: Husband gets mum's sister in trouble

parts.note: your mother's sister is your aunt

explanation.surface: A husband lands his wife's sibling in difficulty.
explanation.definitionFit: To haunt someone is to trouble them persistently, as memories or ghosts do.

clue.text: Enliven by topping with one pizza ingredient

parts.note: to pep up is to enliven
per means by, as in per hour
on means on top of
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Livening up a pizza by putting one topping on it.
explanation.definitionFit: This spicy sausage is a common pizza topping, an example of an ingredient.

clue.text: In Natal he represented Hawthorne for example

indicators.note: represented means presented anew, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone in Natal stood in for a person called Hawthorne.
explanation.walkthrough: Nathaniel Hawthorne was the American author of The Scarlet Letter.
explanation.definitionFit: The novelist Hawthorne's first name exemplifies that forename.

clue.text: Very soon scoundrel gets a girlfriend

parts.note: in a mo, short for in a moment, means very soon
a rat is a scoundrel

explanation.surface: Before long a rogue finds himself a girlfriend.
explanation.definitionFit: An inamorata is a woman someone loves, a female lover or sweetheart.

clue.text: One departure after another for Spaniard

parts.note: to die is to depart this life
to go is another word for departing

explanation.surface: A Spanish man leaves one place after another.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a common Spanish man's given name, so it suits a Spaniard.

clue.text: Bandit's gone round holding sellers up

indicators.note: holding means containing, so one word sits inside the other

parts.note: dead means gone

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word reads upwards, backwards

parts.note: reps are sales representatives
O is round in shape

explanation.surface: An outlaw has gone round with traders in tow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bandit's' is 'Bandit is', the 's a link. 'gone round' tempts as one phrase, but 'round' stands alone as O; 'up' turns the sellers upward in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: A desperado is a reckless outlaw, a synonym of bandit.

clue.text: Something incomprehensible from Tsipras say

definitions.meaning: as in 'it's all ... to me', meaning unintelligible
Alexis Tsipras was prime minister of Greece, so things from him are of that nation

explanation.surface: Something baffling said by the former Greek prime minister.
explanation.definitionFit: The saying 'it's all Greek to me' makes the language stand for gibberish; Tsipras is a national of Greece.

clue.text: Record first signs of indigestion creaking in guts

parts.note: to enter data is to record it

indicators.note: the first signs of words are their initial letters

explanation.surface: Noting early symptoms of dyspepsia as the stomach creaks.
explanation.definitionFit: Enteric means relating to the intestines, so located in the guts.

clue.text: Fool succeeded with heartless gibe about single aide

indicators.note: about means around, so the fool and succeeded go around the single letter

parts.note: an ass is a fool
S is the abbreviation for succeeded in genealogies
I, the Roman numeral, is a single one

indicators.note: heartless means the middle letter is removed

parts.note: a taunt is a gibe

explanation.surface: A fool took over after jeering at an unmarried helper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heartless' removes U from TAUNT, giving TANT.
explanation.definitionFit: An assistant is a helper, a synonym of aide.

clue.text: Big plot last from Zola on prison guards

indicators.note: the last from a word is its final letter
guards means encloses, so the prison word goes around the other

parts.note: a cage is a prison
re means on, about or concerning

explanation.surface: The ending of a Zola story set in a jail, with warders.
explanation.definitionFit: Acreage is an area of land measured in acres, so a big plot.

clue.text: Infamous old port guarded by other people?

indicators.note: guarded by means enclosed by, so these letters go inside

parts.note: other people are 'not us', a cryptic reading
Rio de Janeiro is a Brazilian port

explanation.surface: A disreputable old harbour protected by outsiders.
explanation.definitionFit: Notorious means widely known for something bad, a synonym of infamous.

clue.text: Lordless swordsman right ahead skinned mink

parts.note: on means ahead, as in go on

indicators.note: skinned means the outer letters are stripped off

explanation.surface: A masterless samurai pushes on and skins an animal.
explanation.definitionFit: A ronin was a samurai with no master in feudal Japan.

clue.text: Wet work agent accepts

indicators.note: accepts means takes in, so one word goes inside the other

parts.note: a spy is a secret agent
OP is short for opus, a work

explanation.surface: A secret operative agrees to a damp assignment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wet work' suggests an assassination, but 'Wet' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Wet means feeble or sentimental, which soppy also describes.

clue.text: Mysterious European Republic wanting revolution

indicators.note: wanting revolution means needing to be turned around, so the word reads backwards

parts.note: Eire is the Irish name for the Republic of Ireland

explanation.surface: A puzzling European state that doesn't want an uprising.
explanation.definitionFit: Eerie means strange and unsettling, so mysterious.

clue.text: Lilac no good planted in troubled country

indicators.note: planted in means set inside, so these letters go within

parts.note: Syria is a country beset by conflict

explanation.surface: Lilac fails to flourish when grown in a war-torn land.
explanation.definitionFit: Syringa is the botanical genus name of the lilac.

clue.text: King Henry having an artist over in boozer

indicators.note: in places the group of letters inside the pub abbreviation

parts.note: PH stands for public house, a boozer
H is the abbreviation for henry, the unit of inductance
an is the article A
RA is a Royal Academician, an artist
O is the cricket abbreviation for an over

explanation.surface: A king called Henry drinks with a painter in the pub.
explanation.walkthrough: A boozer is British slang for a pub; 'over' is O, not a reversal.
explanation.definitionFit: A pharaoh was a king of ancient Egypt.

clue.text: Lower form runs new school

parts.note: secondary means lesser, lower in rank
a mode is a form or manner
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A junior class runs a newly built school.
explanation.walkthrough: A secondary modern was a British state school for pupils who did not pass the eleven-plus exam.
explanation.definitionFit: This was a type of British state school, so an example of a school.
